137. In some parts of Wales, people who are not Welsh-speaking employ Welsh idioms when
speaking English. For instance, whereas in English one buys a ticket to travel, the Welsh

idiom is “codi tocyn”– literally “to raise a ticket”. The idiom “raise a ticket” in English is widely
used in parts of Wales by persons who do not speak Welsh.

138. Welsh, like other languages, achieves politeness and avoids undue familiarity in
communication by the use of the second person plural (in Welsh “chi” rather than the
singular “ti”, which is used when addressing the Deity, children, close friends and animals).
A Welsh speaker may, for instance, rely on the polite form of address in making a request
rather than inserting “please” in the utterance. In translation, this distinction may be lost.
